storm.summary_layperson: No storms anywhere nearby tonight — a dry, sunny, breezy northwest flow with nothing on radar, so the cove has no storm risk this evening.
storm.local_effect_blurb: The Sound (61°F) is only about 5°F cooler than the air at 4 PM, and that gap is gone by sunset as the air cools into the mid-50s — no marine-layer effect in play, and none needed with no storms around.
storm.detail_html:
Regional picture: The KOKX radar shows no echoes anywhere in range, there are no NWS watches, warnings or advisories, and the atmosphere is completely stable — 0 J/kg of CAPE (no fuel for thunderstorms) with only 13 kt of wind shear. The air is very dry (dewpoint in the mid-30s, humidity around 30%) behind a cool northwest flow. The Weather Service forecast is simply “Sunny.”

Local effect: Normally the cool Long Island Sound can blunt incoming storms by keeping a stable layer of cool air over the water. That needs the air to be at least ~5°F warmer than the water. This afternoon the cove reads 66°F against 61°F water — right at the threshold — and the Sound holds its temperature while the air cools after sunset (6:03 PM), so the gap closes completely by early evening as the air drops into the mid-50s. With no storms to deflect, this is academic tonight.

Most likely outcome: A dry, clear evening across the cove and surrounding towns alike. No difference between the shoreline and inland areas on the storm front.

What would change the call: Nothing in the current data points toward convection — it would take a new system arriving from the west, which neither radar nor the short-range model shows through tonight.

wind.regime_label: Moderate northerly gradient wind — no sea breeze
wind.tactics_blurb: Northerly breeze blowing off the land — gusty, puffy and shifty with 15–30° swings, so no side is paying on geography alone. Start mid-line, stay near the middle, and tack on the headers while watching upwind for dark puff lines coming off the shore.
wind.tactics_detail_html:
Regime call: This is a moderate gradient-wind day with no sea breeze in play. The air over the cove is only about 5°F warmer than the 61°F Sound water this afternoon, and the wind is blowing off the land from the north-northwest — none of the shoreline stations show any southerly sea-breeze component. A gradient wind like this doesn’t depend on the sun, so it holds through sunset (6:03 PM) rather than collapsing.

Strength: The Riverside YC anemometer reads 14 kt gusting 21 from due north at 4 PM, and the Weather Service has northwest winds around 15 kt. The short-range model (HRRR) is running about 5 kt light against that, so the table is scaled to the observed wind rather than the raw model. Expect it to ease only 2–3 kt after dark as the air near the surface settles — still around 11 kt with mid-teens puffs at 10 PM.

Direction and shifts: Mostly NNW (330–345°) through the window. The model runs about 15–20° left of what the cove is actually seeing (RYC is at 360°), so lean on the righty side of the forecast directions early. A north-northwest wind in the cove comes over the land, so it arrives in puffs and holes with big 15–30° oscillations — the hardest kind of racing, with big gains and losses on every shift.

Tactics: No side is consistently favored, so stay in the middle of the course and play the shifts — tack on the headers and keep your head out of the boat looking for darker puff lines coming off the Greenwich shore. Avoid getting pinned on either layline early; a single good shift is worth more than the side tonight.

What racers will feel: A full-hiking, depowered breeze at the start (14 kt with 20 kt puffs) easing to a comfortable 11–12 kt by the last race. Cold and dry — air in the mid-50s by 8 PM — so dress for it.
